# Kapture

> Kapture is a screenshot capture and visual library product in two parts.
> Kapture for Chrome captures a complete webpage, or a selected area of one, and
> saves it on the user's own device as a PNG, JPEG or PDF. Kapture Pro is a
> desktop screenshot manager that turns the captures already on the user's
> computer into a searchable visual library, organised with Projects,
> Collections and a Smart workspace.

## Products and availability

- **Kapture for Chrome** is released and free. It requires Google Chrome 120 or
  later and is installed from the Chrome Web Store.
- **Kapture Pro for Mac** is planned and has not been released. There is no
  download and no price.
- **Kapture Pro for Windows** is planned and has not been released. There is no
  download and no price.

Kapture Pro is one product that will run on both desktop platforms. Where the
platform does not matter it is called simply Kapture Pro.

## Kapture for Chrome

Kapture runs in Chrome's side panel. In full page mode it scrolls the whole
document rather than capturing only the visible viewport, splitting very long
pages into sections of up to 8,000 image rows. In select area mode the user
drags over the visible page, with Freeform, 1:1, 16:9 and 9:16 ratios. Files
save as PNG, JPEG or PDF.

Files are saved through Chrome's own Downloads system, into a Downloads
subfolder the user names per capture, so different pages or projects can be kept
in different folders. The panel keeps a local capture history split into Kept and
Deleted, offers light and dark themes, and has viewport presets for phone,
tablet and desktop widths. Settings holds the language choice and a link to Help.

## Kapture Pro

Kapture Pro indexes the screenshots already saved on the user's computer. The
files never move and are never uploaded.

Its Library holds All Captures, Recents, Favorites, Desktop Screenshots, Smart
and Collections. Projects sit alongside the Library.

- **Projects** are the primary working structure, one per piece of work in hand.
  Any folder inside the Kapture folder becomes a project automatically.
- **Collections** are part of the Library and group captures the user wants kept
  together, whichever project they came from.
- **Smart** is one workspace with five tools: **Unorganised** (captures not in a
  project yet), **Duplicates** (files identical byte for byte), **Cleanup**
  (older and larger captures worth a second look), **Sources** (captures grouped
  by where they came from) and **Rules** (filing the user asked for). Smart never
  deletes anything.
- **Inspector** shows size, format, dimensions, source and capture time, plus
  tags and notes the user adds.

## Languages

Both products are available in five languages: English, Spanish, Simplified
Chinese, Korean and Japanese. Both also offer a System / Default option that
follows the operating system or browser language. System / Default is a setting,
not a sixth language.

## Data handling

Kapture is local-first. Capturing, storing and organising the library all happen
on the user's own machine, and the core capture and organisation features work
without requiring cloud AI. Screenshots, webpage content, URLs and history
metadata are not sent to the developer or to external servers. There is no
account, no cloud sync, no analytics, no advertising, no tracking and no remote
code.

## Pages

- [Home](https://kaptapp.com/): what Kapture is, the two capture modes, formats, viewport presets, folders, history, themes, Projects, Collections, Smart, languages and common questions.
- [Screenshot organizer](https://kaptapp.com/screenshot-organizer/): how Kapture Pro organises a screenshot library, and the difference between Projects and Collections.
- [Help](https://kaptapp.com/help/): how to use Kapture, permissions and release notes for the Chrome extension.
- [Privacy Policy](https://kaptapp.com/privacy/): what information Kapture handles, how it is stored locally, and what is never transmitted.

Spanish, Simplified Chinese, Korean and Japanese versions of the home, help and
privacy pages live under /es/, /zh/, /ko/ and /ja/.
